title: Limit cycles
input_latex: x' = - x \left(x^{2} + y^{2}\right) + x - y,\qquad y' = x - y \left(x^{2} + y^{2}\right) + y
normal_latex: x' = - x \left(x^{2} + y^{2}\right) + x - y,\qquad y' = x - y \left(x^{2} + y^{2}\right) + y
summary: Limit cycles of a planar system. A circular limit cycle was found.

methods.name: Bendixson's criterion
methods.reason: A quick test that can rule closed orbits out.

steps.title: Compute the divergence
steps.text: Bendixson's criterion: if \(f_x + g_y\) is not zero and keeps one sign throughout a region without holes, no closed orbit lies entirely inside it.

steps.title: Conclude
steps.text: The divergence changes sign across the curve \(- 4 x^{2} - 4 y^{2} + 2 = 0\). No closed orbit can lie entirely on one side of that curve, but one may cross it, so closed orbits are not ruled out.

steps.title: Result
latex: \text{Closed orbits are possible only if they cross } - 4 x^{2} - 4 y^{2} + 2 = 0.

methods.particular_latex: \text{Closed orbits are possible only if they cross } - 4 x^{2} - 4 y^{2} + 2 = 0.

methods.name: Polar coordinates
methods.reason: The radial equation separates from the angle, so circular limit cycles can be read off.

steps.title: Change to polar coordinates
steps.text: Use \(r\,r' = x\,x' + y\,y'\) and \(r^{2}\theta' = x\,y' - y\,x'\) with \(x = r\cos\theta\), \(y = r\sin\theta\).

steps.title: Find the circular orbits
steps.text: A circle \(r = r_0\) is a closed orbit when \(r' = 0\) there and the angle keeps turning. It attracts nearby solutions when \(r'\) is positive just inside and negative just outside.

steps.title: Check
steps.text: Checked that r' = 0 on each circle found.

methods.verify_note: Checked that r' = 0 on each circle found.

methods.name: Liénard's theorem
methods.reason: It applies to equations \(x'' + f(x)\,x' + g(x) = 0\), written as \(x' = y\), \(y' = -g(x) - f(x)\,y\). This system is not of that form.
